full_judgment: 20. Further he goes to submit that the heading of the definition of "zero rated goods and services " as contained in section 2(5) of the VAT Act, 1991 is a camouflage as the heading, if read in isolation, gives an impression as if those goods and services are, in fact, taxable but assessed at zero rate for the time being. However, from a plain reading of the said definition it transpires that the Legislature has completely prohibited imposition of any VAT on any exported or deemed to be exported goods and services. The prohibition of taxation on such goods and services is even more stringent than that of the exemption as the Legislature delegated no authority on the government or the Board to put any condition or limitation as opposed to exemption by section 14 of the VAT Act. Therefore, he submits the true impart of section 2(5) is that the exported goods and services are not taxable although the title indicates the opposite. Moreover, section 32 has stipulated issuance of "কর চালানপত্র" VAT invoice in Form "Mushak-19" by every registered person. Conversely, section 35 has provided for submission of "দাখিলপত্র" only by the manufacturer or producer or trader of taxable goods or services.Therefore, inclusion of exported and exempted goods and services in "Mushak -19" by the Board is ultra vires the VAT Act, 1991 which the Legislature neither mentioned nor intended, for, the very purpose of submission of VAT return under Rule 24(3) is to produce a statement of entire VAT liability of the persons doing business of manufacturing or trading of taxable goods and services. Accordingly, he submits that when the exported and exempted goods and services do not create any tax liability on the part of the manufacturer or traders submission of VAT return under the said Rule becomes irrelevant for them. Consequent thereto imposition of fine of Taka 10,000 upon the petitioner for non-submission VAT return in "Mushak-19" is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and hence, is of no legal effect.
